pipeline.note: A refund can be modelled as spending reversal (outflow reduced) or as income. The Forge schema has only inflow/outflow, so the contract reading (refund = inflow) is primary; netting against spend is a valid alternative that changes inflow, outflow and savings rate but not net.
pipeline.description: A refund row (positive amount) alongside the purchase it reverses.

pipeline.note: An own-account transfer is neither income nor spending. The schema has no transfer type, so both legs are counted (contract reading, primary). Excluding internal transfers is a valid alternative that changes inflow, outflow and savings rate but not net.
pipeline.description: A transfer to savings recorded as an outflow plus a matching inflow in the other account.

pipeline.note: months = whole calendar months from first to last date (documented). Months without transactions count toward avgMonthlyNet but are skipped by the stability and trend halves (active months only); averaging over active months only is a valid alternative.
pipeline.description: Activity in Jan, Apr and Sep only (empty months in between).
Year boundary and leap day; first and last months are single-day months.
200 outflows of 0.10: a naive float sum drifts; the exact total is 20.00.
Values around 1e9 with cents.

Separate Debit/Credit columns.
Accounting negatives in parentheses with thousands separators.
Euro-prefixed amounts, no currency column: the dataset currency is EUR.
DD/MM/YYYY dates containing a day > 12 (unambiguous).

Month-name dates.

pipeline.note: All day/month fields are <= 12, so DD/MM and MM/DD are both valid readings. Forge's documented default is DD/MM and it must warn; the truth uses DD/MM.
pipeline.description: Slash dates where no field exceeds 12.
One column mixes 13/02/2024 (DD/MM) and 02/13/2024 (MM/DD): contradictory, must warn.
Seven categories with distinct totals; checks totals, ranking and shares.
Two categories tie exactly; rank-dependent metrics are not eligible (ordering undefined).
No category column: Forge infers categories from descriptions (human labels are the truth).
One non-housing category is 70% of spending.
Six months; dining rises from 100 to 220/month, groceries flat.
Five months: halves of 2 and 3 months must be compared per month, not in total.

pipeline.note: Forge compares halves of the ACTIVE months (months with at least one transaction). Treating the empty calendar months as zero-spend months is a valid alternative that changes every per-month average.
pipeline.description: Active months Jan, Feb, Aug, Sep with a long gap between.
A category appears only in the recent half.
Identical months: nothing changed.
Net cash flow falls by more than half because dining spending rises tenfold.
Net cash flow falls because income halves; spending is flat. The decline is real but is NOT caused by rising spending.
Twelve ordinary grocery charges and one 900 surgery bill.
Ten similar charges; no outlier exists.
Rent of 1500 every month plus ordinary groceries: the rent is regular, not anomalous.
Only four outflows: too little history to call any of them an outlier.
Eight identical 50.00 charges (a subscription): zero variance, nothing is an outlier.

pipeline.note: The documented rule divides by the median absolute deviation, which is 0 when most variable amounts are identical; the numeric flag set is then undefined. The LABEL (10.50 is 5% above its cluster and is not an outlier) is unambiguous.
pipeline.description: Variable spend is 10.00, 10.00, 10.50 plus a 100.00 bill three times (recurring): 10.50 is not an outlier.
Two genuine one-offs among ordinary spending.
Rent 1500 x5 (recurring) and one 3000 deposit (a one-off).
A 0.50 charge among ~50 charges: unusually SMALL is not an anomaly of the 'large charge' type.
The largest outflow is a recurring 2000 rent; the only genuine outlier is a 400 dental bill (4.5% of spending).
A normal household: groceries ~450/month, dining ~100, transport ~60. Monthly groceries are ordinary for this household and must not be flagged just because they dwarf dining and transport.

pipeline.note: Rubric 1.1.0: the ordinary grocery rows are regular monthly spend in a category present in every month, so they are FALSE whatever their ratio to the pooled median (4.4x here, which rubric 1.0.0 left ungraded). The 2,600 order is 25x the pooled median and is not ordinary for its own category, so it is TRUE. insight:anomaly-impact is left ungraded: the one-off is 15.4% of total outflow, inside the 5-20% band.
pipeline.description: Groceries recur monthly at ~470 with no two amounts alike, and one month also carries a 2,600 bulk order. The ordinary rows are regular spend; the 2,600 is a genuine one-off and must still be flagged.

pipeline.note: Written to catch the opposite error from D-an-011. Travel appears in only two months, which is not a recurring commitment, so its rows stay candidates: Flights is 15.6x the pooled median (TRUE) and Rail pass is 1.43x (FALSE, under the 1.5x bound). If a rule excluded whole categories from the baseline rather than only from candidacy, the baseline here would collapse to two amounts and Flights could stop being flagged.
pipeline.description: Travel appears in only two of six months, while groceries and dining recur in all six.

pipeline.note: No category column, so Forge must infer all 16 categories from real-looking bank strings: abbreviations (AMZN, S/MKT), trailing store and reference numbers, and the same merchant written three ways. The truth categories are the human reading of each line. Expected to be hard; whatever it scores is the honest state of category inference on real descriptions.
pipeline.description: Four months of one current account with no category column and bank-style merchant strings.

pipeline.note: Two accounts in one period, including a same-day own-account transfer pair (out of current, into savings). Whether an own-account transfer belongs in inflow/outflow is already listed as interpretation-dependent in §6.4; this case states the contract reading, which counts what the rows say.
pipeline.description: A current account and a savings account over three months, with monthly transfers between them.

pipeline.note: A statement that begins on the 19th and ends on the 9th, so the first and last months are partial — the calendar-vs-active-month averaging question in §6.4 applies. Also carries a purchase split into three instalments and a partial refund against an earlier purchase.
pipeline.description: Statement running 19 Jan to 9 Apr: partial first and last months, an instalment plan, and a partial refund.

pipeline.note: The same ticker held in two accounts is one economic position. Forge treats every row as its own position (no aggregation by symbol), which lowers HHI. Both readings are defensible; the contract (one holding row = one position) is primary.
pipeline.description: VTI appears twice (two accounts).

Fund wrappers: a money-market fund is cash; a bond ETF is fixed income; a gold ETF is a commodity.

Cash equals exactly one month of average spending: runway = 1.0 (cap boundary is strict < 1).
Holdings but no cash: runway 0.
Cash covers 24 months: liquidity sub-score saturates at 1.

pipeline.note: DECISIONS D8 and PROJECT_RULES say the score is capped at 55 when a MAJORITY of months are negative. With 3 of 5 months negative (60%) the cap applies. This case was interpretation-dependent under dataset 1.0.0, because the code then capped only when fewer than 34% of months were non-negative; D21 settled the question in favour of the documented rule and the code implements it, so the expected score of 55 is now the single reading. The expected value has not changed.
pipeline.description: Five months, three negative.
Strong liquidity and diversification but spending exceeds income: score capped at 45.
Holdings with no transactions: no health score, runway unavailable.
Six months, 42% savings, no negative month, 8+ months of cash, diversified.

A single transaction.

Expenses +10%.

All four levers at once.

Baseline has no spending (so no runway); a scenario adds a one-off expense. The runway delta must not be computed against a fabricated baseline of 0.

pipeline.note: 'Recurring monthly expense' is applied by Forge to each month that contains data (documented in simulate.ts). Applying it to every calendar month of the period is a valid alternative.
pipeline.description: Recurring expense on a period with empty months.
Out-of-range / non-finite scenario inputs must be rejected, not turned into negative or infinite amounts.
Rows tagged USD and EUR in one transactions file: must refuse to sum them.
USD transactions with INR holdings (holdings tagged via a Currency column).
Amount cells carry different currency symbols ($ and €) with no currency column: silently summing them would be a mixed-currency total.
Missing date, zero amount, text amount: each skipped with a reason.
Impossible calendar dates (2024-02-30, 2024-13-01) must be rejected, not accepted as-is.
Infinity / NaN / garbage amounts are rejected with a reason.
Negative and zero holding values are skipped with reasons.
A file with a header and no data rows.
Unsupported file extension.
One row has both a Debit (100) and a Credit (40): contradictory. Silently keeping one and dropping the other loses data.
Currency cell says 'Swiss Franc' (not recognised): silently assuming USD would corrupt totals.
Holding states quantity 10 x price 100 but value 5000: contradictory.

Decimal comma or malformed thousands; 15 is not a plausible reading.
Zero-value rows carry no movement and are skipped with a reason (documented).
Unicode minus sign (U+2212), common in PDF/Excel exports: dropping it flips the sign silently.
Ambiguous order; DD/MM is Forge's documented default.
